## The puzzle

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

The 2026 war stabilized at a ceasefire that nobody loves. Now the Gulf is realigning — but in five different directions at once. Bahrain operationally bandwagoned with the US (CSIPA Article II, RAF deployment, 160+ detentions). The UAE exited OPEC and deployed Iron Dome. Saudi *denied* US airspace, signed a formal alliance treaty with Pakistan, and kept Tehran's embassy open. The standard "fragmented hedging" menu has no entry for what Saudi is doing.

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

The 28 February 2026 ceasefire stabilized the war but resolved nothing. Iran's regime survived. The strikes had succeeded operationally and failed strategically — Iran retained the enrichment know-how and the institutional structures to rebuild. Every Gulf state is now realigning in response to the new state, and the realignments do not point in one direction. Bahrain invoked CSIPA Article II on 5 March (first ever), led a 135-state UNSC resolution, hosted RAF Typhoons, and detained 160+ IRGC-linked individuals. The UAE exited OPEC on 1 May, deployed Iron Dome (its first foreign combat use), closed Tehran's embassy day-one of the war. Saudi Arabia — in the same window — *denied* US airspace for Project Freedom, signed a $3bn debt-relief tranche to Pakistan to operationalize the September 2025 [Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement]{.gloss data-gloss="saudi-pakistan-smda"}, accelerated the Turkish KAAN fighter procurement, and kept the Tehran embassy open with Hajj coordination signed. Qatar mediated. Oman declined the GCC summit. The standard five-configuration menu (system-wide US umbrella; fragmented hedging; status quo; Iran-CRINK hard balancing; Saudi-UAE permanent split) has *no entry* for what Saudi is doing. The puzzle Q12.5 sets: what is the actual emerging configuration?

::: {.bottom-line}
**Bottom line.** *The post-war Gulf is fragmenting along three axes simultaneously.* Bahrain (and partially UAE) is operationally bandwagoning with the US-Israel architecture (Configuration A, bilateral only). Saudi is constructing a Sunni-Muslim third pole via Pakistan, Turkey, and a preserved Iran channel ([Configuration F]{.gloss data-gloss="configuration-f-saudi-third-pole"}, posterior **0.40**). Oman, Qatar, and Iraq pursue independent or parallel paths. Configuration F is the most likely single descriptor — but it is not in the standard menu.
:::

## Methodology — six trajectories, five-then-six configurations, the Bahrain test

This chapter applies the project's standard 8-step protocol plus a 9th briefing-review pass. The plan refinement (2026-05-10) specified six trajectory hypotheses (H1–H6) and five joint configurations (A–E); the devil's-advocate pass (Critique 13) forced a sixth — Configuration F (Saudi-led Sunni-Muslim third pole). The Bahrain test was identified as the cleanest single discriminator between the Lim-Cooper-strict bimodal reading (some states bandwagon, others hedge) and the Kuik-broad uniform-hedger reading. Configuration probabilities were renormalized to sum to 1.0 after the DA correction. An Israeli-factions enrichment pass strengthened Configuration F (0.35 → 0.40) by anchoring Saudi-Israel normalization-slipping to the religious-Zionist mathematical veto on Palestinian-state concession.
:::

**Six trajectory hypotheses, drawn from the corpus.** The plan refinement identified six distinct trajectories the Gulf could be on; each is grounded in a specific framework or empirical pattern. *H1 — Bypass acceleration:* the Iran-can-close-Hormuz threat motivates pipeline build-out around the Strait. Petroline at ~7 mb/d nameplate (Saudi); Habshan-Fujairah at ~1.5-1.8 mb/d (UAE); Iraq Basra-Haditha pipeline groundbreaking 1 May 2026 (~$5bn, target 2.5 mb/d via Syria/Turkey/Jordan); Kirkuk-Ceyhan expansion in April. *H2 — GCC consolidation:* the war as catalyst for unified GCC institutional integration. Jeddah summit 28 April 2026 (first in-person since the war began) advanced a joint missile early-warning system; Carnegie called this the "realistic" rather than "hopeful" scenario. *H3 — Fragmentation:* each state on its own trajectory; the GCC becomes an emergent rather than primitive entity. *H4 — Iran-Saudi détente collapse:* the 2023 China-brokered framework dissolves under wartime adversarial pressure. *H5 — [Hedging vs bandwagoning]{.gloss data-gloss="lim-cooper-hedging"}* applied with definitional discipline: H5a is Lim-Cooper-strict (bimodal split — some bandwagon, others hedge) and H5b is Kuik-broad (uniform hedging across all states). *H6 — Deepened US security per [Fulton 2026]{.gloss data-gloss="fulton-alignment"}:* GCC states as interest-based alignment-deepeners with the US, not wait-and-see hedgers. The Bahrain test discriminates H5a vs H5b cleanly.
:::

[**The [Bahrain test]{.gloss data-gloss="bahrain-test"}.** Four observable behaviors — [CSIPA Article II]{.gloss data-gloss="bahrain-csipa"} (first-ever activation, 5 March), 135-state UNSC resolution leadership, RAF Typhoon hosting, and 160+ IRGC-linked detentions — are *all* consistent with operational bandwagoning and *none* are consistent with rhetorical hedging. H5a (Lim-Cooper-strict bimodal split) confirmed; H5b (Kuik-broad uniform hedging) falsified.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**The [Bahrain test]{.gloss data-gloss="bahrain-test"}.** The cleanest single empirical discriminator between the Lim-Cooper-strict bimodal reading (some Gulf states bandwagon, others hedge) and the Kuik-broad uniform-hedger reading. Bahrain's behavior since 28 February 2026 is observable on four dimensions, all going the same way. *Dimension 1 — formal security commitment:* [Bahrain CSIPA Article II invocation]{.gloss data-gloss="bahrain-csipa"} on 5 March 2026 was the first-ever activation of the 2023 US-Bahrain Comprehensive Security Integration and Prosperity Agreement's mutual-consultation provisions. The invocation triggered senior-level Defense Working Group consultations and UK joining via RAF Typhoon deployment to Bahrain — a structural escalation in Gulf-US security architecture. *Dimension 2 — diplomatic leadership:* Bahrain led a 135-state UN Security Council resolution on Iran; this is operational diplomatic *leadership* for the US-aligned position, not wait-and-see hedging. *Dimension 3 — military hosting:* RAF Typhoon deployment is the kind of visible commitment hedgers explicitly avoid. *Dimension 4 — domestic security:* 160+ IRGC-linked detentions inside Bahrain during the war period (Carnegie / Al-Monitor / Middle East Eye reporting) are a domestic alignment commitment a hedging state would not make. All four observable behaviors are consistent with operational bandwagoning; none is consistent with rhetorical hedging. H5a confirmed decisively; H5b falsified.
:::

**[Configuration F (NEW): Saudi-led Sunni-Muslim third pole construction]{.gloss data-gloss="configuration-f-saudi-third-pole"}.** Saudi behavior since 28 February 2026 fits no entry in the original five-configuration menu. The pattern: *Pakistan* — the September 2025 [Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement]{.gloss data-gloss="saudi-pakistan-smda"} is a formal alliance treaty (mutual-defense obligations, strategic-asset coordination, implicit Pakistani-nuclear-umbrella reach), operationalized post-war with $3bn Saudi debt relief in April-May 2026. *Turkey* — the KAAN fighter procurement is in advanced negotiation (Atlantic Council Hausheer Ali / Al-Monitor sourcing); FM Faisal in Ankara 6 May 2026 coordinated next steps. *US-independence signaling* — Saudi denied Project Freedom airspace 5-7 May 2026, a clientelist signal that the patron had requested action without consultation. *Iran channel preservation* — Tehran embassy kept open, Hajj 2026 coordination signed, ~30,000 pilgrims arrived Medina by 27 April. The four together fit Walt's [balance-of-threat]{.gloss data-gloss="walt-balance-of-threat"} framework with the additional prediction (drawn from Snyder's [abandonment-vs-entrapment]{.gloss data-gloss="snyder-abandonment-entrapment"} under acute multipolar conditions) that small or middle states facing an unreliable patron will form *alternative* alliance structures rather than passively hedge. [Lim-Cooper's hedging discipline]{.gloss data-gloss="lim-cooper-hedging"} explicitly excludes treaty-level commitments from "hedging" — this is alliance formation. The Lim-Cooper framework has no analytical room for third-pole construction; its binary (hedge between two great powers vs bandwagon with one) does not capture three-pole dynamics where a middle state *builds* the third pole.
:::

**Israeli inner-coalition structural lock-in reinforces Configuration F (0.35 → 0.40).** The Iran-war briefing's Round 9 finding on Israeli factions substantially refines Q12.5 by showing the hawkish posture is structurally locked in, not contingent on any one Netanyahu coalition. Four components: *the [Hesder pipeline]{.gloss data-gloss="hesder-pipeline"}* — religious-Zionist yeshiva-IDF combined-service graduates make up roughly one-third of infantry officers and half of combat-officer-school graduates, progressively replacing the historically secular-pragmatist Ashkenazi officer corps. *The Mizrahi-Shas-Likud electoral bond* — since 1977, the Mizrahi-Likud political reservoir has been "the bond making 2026 Iran posture electorally sustainable" (briefing language). *Cohen-to-Barnea Mossad reversal* — the institutional shift to hawkish doctrine across the 2016-2025 period made Rising Lion (early 2025) and the 28 February 2026 strikes operationally possible. *2024-25 systematic dismantling* — Haliva/Halevi/Finkelman + Gallant/Bar firings destroyed the institutional architecture for pragmatist veto. For Q12.5, the implication is: Saudi's reading of US patron unreliability is *reinforced* by the recognition that bilateral US assurance cannot insulate Saudi from Israeli unilateralism *if* Israeli unilateralism is structurally durable. The Saudi calculus shifts *more* toward third-pole construction. (The [Q11]{.column-margin} DA dormant-vs-destroyed caveat — pragmatist faction operates publicly via Hayman/INSS, Haaretz security-chiefs, Bennett-Lapid polling — caps the Configuration F upper bound at 0.45 rather than rising further.)

[The system-level pattern is therefore: bilateral Configuration A for Bahrain (operationally) + UAE (partially); Configuration F for Saudi specifically; independent / parallel patterns for Oman, Qatar, Iraq; Kuwait under-determined. *Bilateral patterns do not aggregate to system-wide A* — the GCC is *not* consolidating as an institutional integrator. Configuration F captures the most analytically distinctive Saudi-specific dynamic.]{.column-margin}

### Figure 5 — Source-confidence audit

Of the synthesis's load-bearing claims:

- **[T1]{.tier .tier-1} multi-source verified:** [Bahrain CSIPA Article II 5 March]{.gloss data-gloss="bahrain-csipa"} (Modern Diplomacy + L'Europeista); Bahrain 135-state UNSC resolution (Gulf International Forum + multiple); Bahrain 160+ detentions (Carnegie Wehrey/Johnson + multiple); UAE OPEC exit 1 May (Al Jazeera + WaPo + multiple); UAE-Iran Mansour-Ghalibaf call April 15 (Al-Monitor + Arab News); [Saudi-Pakistan SMDA Sept 2025]{.gloss data-gloss="saudi-pakistan-smda"} as formal alliance treaty (Wikipedia + primary sources); $3bn Saudi-Pakistan debt April; Saudi airspace denial May 5-7 (NBC + Jewish Insider); Saudi Tehran embassy kept open (AGSIW); Iran-Saudi Hajj 2026 coordination (Mehr News + Gulf News); Trump-Xi summit May 14-15 with Iran central (CNBC + CSIS + CFR).
- **[T2]{.tier .tier-2} single-source named:** Saudi-Turkey KAAN deal advanced negotiation (Atlantic Council Hausheer Ali + Al-Monitor); MBS regime-change-preferable private (WaPo + PBS, US officials only — Saudi denies); Oman absent Jeddah summit (The National attendance roster); UAE OPEC exit reading as US-alignment signal (Ziemba CNAS + Mazarei PIIE — alternatives unranked); Saudi-Israel normalization "slipping" (MEI commentary).
- **[T3]{.tier .tier-3} inference from evidence:** **[Configuration F]{.gloss data-gloss="configuration-f-saudi-third-pole"} as the most plausible Saudi reading** (analyst inference from converging T1 evidence; the central load-bearing claim); US patron reliability *contested* not established (DA #9 inference); H4 = PARTIAL TRUE (détente eroding in substance, façade preserved); Configuration F probability 0.40 (analyst posterior; sensitive to Trump-Xi outcome and SMDA operational follow-through).
- **[T4]{.tier .tier-4} conjecture:** none in the load-bearing path.

The single highest-load-bearing T3 inference is Configuration F. The underlying empirical anchors are T1, but the *framework swap* — reading Saudi behavior through Walt + Snyder rather than through Lim-Cooper-hedging — is the inferential leap. **Sharpest risk to synthesis**: if Saudi-Pakistan SMDA proves to be paper agreement without operational follow-through, Configuration F collapses and Saudi reverts to Configuration B (state-by-state hedging) or weak Configuration A.

## Pre-mortem {#pre-mortem}

If this synthesis is wrong, the most likely failure modes are:

1. **Configuration F overstated.** Saudi-Pakistan SMDA might be paper agreement without operational follow-through. KAAN deal might collapse on financing or technical issues. Saudi airspace denial might be reversed within months. If all three, Configuration F collapses to Configuration B (Saudi as hedger) or weak Configuration A. Watch for joint Saudi-Pakistan exercises, intelligence-sharing announcements, Pakistani strategic-asset deployment to Saudi territory.

2. **US patron reliability reading wrong direction.** Bahrain's aggressive CSIPA invocation might reflect actual US-demonstrated reliability via behind-the-scenes commitments not in public data. If so, Configuration A pattern extends from Bahrain to UAE/Qatar/Saudi over 12-18 months. Watch for classified US-Gulf agreements, intelligence-sharing protocols, military prepositioning announcements.

3. **Configuration F is correct for Saudi specifically but doesn't generalize.** Saudi might be constructing a third pole alone, not as part of a Gulf-wide configuration. UAE/Qatar/Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman not joining Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey axis. If so, Configuration F is a Saudi-specific deviation from system-level Configuration B. Track which Gulf states actively participate in Saudi-led architecture.

4. **Trump-Xi summit (May 14-15) produces unexpectedly large structural deliverable.** A China-mediated Iran nuclear framework + Hormuz reopening + Taiwan arms-sale restraint would reduce Saudi abandonment anxiety, weaken Configuration F urgency.

5. **Israeli action during MOU window collapses ceasefire.** Re-tests US patron reliability in real time. If US fails to defend Saudi/Gulf during retaliation cascade, Configuration F accelerates dramatically. If US succeeds, Configuration A regains ground.

6. **Iranian regime cohesion fractures.** If IRGC-Vahidi-Ghalibaf split materializes, Iran becomes leaderless; Saudi's Iran-channel insurance collapses; Configuration F's third-leg breaks down.

## How to read the tier badges

[T1]{.tier .tier-1} **Multi-source verified.** Independent corroboration from at least two distinct sources of different type.

[T2]{.tier .tier-2} **Single-source named.** Reported by one named source. Not yet independently corroborated.

[T3]{.tier .tier-3} **Inference from evidence.** A reading of empirical evidence under a chosen analytical framework. The factual base is supported but the inferential leap is the analyst's.

[T4]{.tier .tier-4} **Conjecture.** A working hypothesis not yet supported by either named source or strong inference.
